title: multi-tenant-otlp-fanout-with-dynamic-credential-rotation-and-backpressure-buffering
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Build a robust OTLP fanout path that supports multi-tenant routing to multiple tracing backends (Tempo, Jaeger, third-party SaaS), adds safe local buffering with on-disk spillover, and rotates exporter credentials without dropping spans. This ticket implements a credential rotation flow for per-tenant exporter credentials, integrates backpressure signals from downstream exporters to the ingest path, and exposes metrics and alerts for backlog growth and spillover activity.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant exporter credentials can be rotated without losing in-flight spans (zero-downtime rotation test pass)
The fanout path can route spans to Tempo and Jaeger simultaneously with configurable per-tenant backoff policies

When downstream exporter reports backpressure or transient failures, spans are buffered in memory up to a safe threshold and then spilled to disk; no spans are dropped during a simulated 10 minute backend outage
Metrics for per-tenant buffer size, disk spillover bytes, exporter backoff state, and rotation events are emitted and available in the observability stack
New dashboards/playbooks documenting operations for buffer alerts and credential rotation are added to Console
E2E integration tests cover normal flow, backend outage, credential rotation during outage, and recovery with no data loss
technical_notes: Design choices: 1) Use a dual-writer fanout: primary synchronous path to preferred backend with async replication to secondary backends to reduce tail latency. 2) Implement an exporter-credential-manager that watches KMS-sealed credentials and provides atomic swaps; credentials cached with versioned tokens and grace TTL to drain in-flight requests. 3) Backpressure propagation: exporters expose a simple status API (ok | throttled | unhealthy) and the relay uses an exponential backoff per-tenant; on throttled, switch to async buffer+spill. 4) Buffering strategy: in-memory ring buffer per-tenant with configurable max_records and max_bytes; when exceeded, spill to per-tenant file segments with append-only writes and compaction during recovery. 5) Observability: instrument counters/gauges and histograms for backlog_latency_ms, buffer_records_count, disk_spill_segments, exporter_retry_count. 6) Security: KMS/HSM integration for credential unsealing and rotation audit logs required for private deployments.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal build and unit tests on canary cluster. Phase 2: Deploy to staging with synthetic span generator targeting a single non-critical tenant and Tempo only. Phase 3: Enable multi-backend fanout in staging and run fault injection (drop/latency/backpressure). Phase 4: Gradual rollout to hosted infra: 5% of traffic for 24h, then 25%, 50% with close monitoring of buffer metrics. Final: flip for all tenants. Feature flag gating: otlp.multitenant.fanout_v2 and otlp.credential_rotation.enabled. Abort conditions: sustained per-tenant disk_spill_segments > 5 for 30m or error rate > 2% for 1h.
test_plan: Unit tests for credential manager and buffer lifecycle. Integration tests: 1) rotate credentials while sending 100k spans/s and assert no loss; 2) simulate Tempo outage for 15m and assert in-memory->disk spill and subsequent replay restores order; 3) backpressure simulation by toggling exporter status API to 'throttled' and verifying relay honors exponential backoff and metrics expose state. Add chaos tests to break file system permissions and ensure safe failure modes. Create an automated nightly job that runs the credential rotation scenario.
